parts.label: a
parts.technique: Trig identity proof using compound angle/double angle formulae (P5.6, P5.8)
parts.reason: Deriving sin3θ using sin(2θ+θ) expansion and double angle formulae is standard proof of trig identity, covered by P5.6 (sin(A+B) formulae, double angle) and P5.8 (construct proofs involving trig identities). Not excluded by P5.6's tan(θ/2) exclusion.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Exact value evaluation using derived identity
parts.reason: Simple substitution into a known trig identity to get exact value, consistent with P5.3/P5.6 use of exact values.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Algebraic manipulation of rational expressions to common denominator
parts.reason: Combining fractions with denominators (x+2) and (x+2)^2 to a single fraction is standard algebraic manipulation covered by P2.6 (rational expressions, algebraic division).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Completing the square to show quadratic always positive
parts.reason: Completing the square for x^2+x+1 to show positivity is explicitly covered by P2.3.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Combining results to deduce sign of f(x)
parts.reason: Uses results from (a) and (b), both in-spec algebra/quadratic topics, to deduce f(x)>0; a simple logical deduction consistent with proof by deduction (P1.1).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Verifying a point lies on a parametric curve
parts.reason: Substituting y=π/4 into x=2siny to verify the given point lies on curve is basic parametric equation work, covered by P3.3.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Implicit/parametric differentiation to find dy/dx
parts.reason: Differentiating x=2siny with respect to y and inverting to find dy/dx is implicit differentiation for first derivative, covered by P7.5.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Equation of normal to curve at a point
parts.reason: Using gradient from (b) and perpendicular gradient condition to find normal line equation, covered by P7.3 (tangents/normals) and P7.5 (curves given parametrically).

parts.label: i
parts.technique: Quotient rule differentiation and finding stationary points
parts.reason: Differentiating y=x/(9+x^2) using the quotient rule and solving dy/dx=0 to find turning points is standard, covered by P7.4 (quotient rule) and P7.3 (stationary points).

parts.label: ii
parts.technique: Chain rule differentiation of composite exponential function
parts.reason: Differentiating y=(1+e^{2x})^{3/2} using the chain rule and evaluating at a given x is covered by P7.4 (chain rule) and P7.2 (differentiating e^{kx}).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Expressing a cosx+b sinx in the form Rsin(x+α)
parts.reason: Explicitly covered by P5.6 (a cosθ + b sinθ in equivalent forms).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Solving trigonometric equation in given interval
parts.reason: Solving R sin(x+α)=1 for x in a given range is standard, covered by P5.7 (solve trig equations in a given interval) using the P5.6 result.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Finding inverse function and its domain
parts.reason: Finding f^{-1} for ln(4-2x) by changing subject is standard inverse function work, covered by P2.8 and P6.3 (ln as inverse of e^x).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Finding range of inverse function
parts.reason: Range of f^{-1} follows from domain/range relationship of inverse functions, covered by P2.8.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Sketching graph of an inverse function with intercepts
parts.reason: Sketching y=f^{-1}(x) and finding axis intercepts is covered by P2.8 (graphs of inverse functions) and P2.7 (sketching curves, intersection points).

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Iteration using recurrence relation x_{n+1}=g(x_n)
parts.reason: Calculating iterates of a given iterative formula to given decimal places is explicitly covered by P9.2/P9.3.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Using iteration to find an approximate root to given accuracy
parts.reason: Continuing iteration (or sign-change check) to find k to required accuracy is covered by P9.2/P9.3 and P9.1 (change of sign methods) as alternative.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Locating a root by sign change
parts.reason: Showing f(-2) and f(-1) have opposite signs to locate a root is explicitly covered by P9.1.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Finding turning point via differentiation
parts.reason: Differentiating quartic and solving f'(x)=0 for stationary point is covered by P7.3.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Polynomial division/factor theorem to find constants
parts.reason: Given f(x)=(x-2)(x^3+ax^2+bx+c), comparing coefficients to find a,b,c is covered by P2.6 (factor theorem, algebraic division of cubics).

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Sketching graph of a quartic function
parts.reason: Sketching y=f(x) for a quartic is explicitly covered by P2.7 (curves including quartic functions).

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Sketching modulus graph y=|f(x)| from y=f(x)
parts.reason: P2.9 guidance explicitly states students should be able to sketch y=|f(x)| given the graph of y=f(x), extending beyond the linear-only case in P2.7.

parts.label: i
parts.technique: Proving a trig identity using sec^2/cosec^2 relations
parts.reason: Using sec²x=1+tan²x and cosec²x=1+cot²x to prove the identity is explicitly covered by P5.5 and P5.8.

parts.label: ii(a)
parts.technique: Expressing arcsin x in terms of y using arccos relationship
parts.reason: Working with arccos and arcsin definitions and their relationship is explicitly covered by P5.4.

parts.reason: Follows directly from P5.4 definitions/relationships of inverse trig functions.
